clue.text: One puts you under the sea, moving in opposing way

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: anti means against or opposing
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the letters of the sea are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle about something that carries you beneath the waves while travelling in the contrary direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the sea' reads as one phrase, but 'under' ends the definition: being put under is being made unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical specialist who sends patients unconscious before surgery is said to put them under.

clue.text: Stirs drinks after leaving clubs

indicators.note: the drinking word is wanted once the clubs letter has gone out of it

parts.note: to carouse is to drink heavily and merrily
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated by drinking after a night out at the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leaving' removes C from CAROUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse feelings or a sleeper is to stir them; both verbs share the sense of waking or exciting.

clue.text: Radical failed to secure new stronghold for the Reds

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the new letter safely inside them
radical change reworks the letters of failed thoroughly

explanation.surface: A political radical has failed to hold a fresh fortress for left-wing Reds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' rearranges FAILED to AFIELD, and 'to secure' holds N inside it after the first A. Anfield is Liverpool FC's stadium, and Liverpool are nicknamed the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's home ground is their fortress, the stadium where the Reds are hardest to beat.

clue.text: International sportsman bowled between well and fine

indicators.note: the bowled letter goes between the two other pieces

parts.note: a spring is a natural well or source of water
OK means fine, all right
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled out, landing somewhere between fine and well.
explanation.walkthrough: A Springbok is a player for South Africa's national rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: Players capped by South Africa at rugby are called Springboks, after the antelope on their emblem.

clue.text: Big serpent in flowery bushes up to the middle

indicators.note: only the first half of the shrub's name is kept, as far as its midpoint

parts.note: hydrangeas are flowering shrubs

explanation.surface: A large snake lurking in garden shrubs, buried up to its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to the middle' keeps the first five of the ten letters of HYDRANGEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra of Greek myth was a huge many-headed water snake slain by Heracles.

clue.text: Decorative tile son fixed up over time

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first part above the time word
in a down clue, up says these letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
set means fixed, settled
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A craftsman's son mounts an ornamental tile, taking a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads letters from the bottom, and 'over' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square pieces of stone or glass used in mosaic work.

clue.text: Strength enlivens revolutionary saving energy

indicators.note: saving means except, so the energy letter is left out
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: animates means brings to life, enlivens
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A political radical gains strength by conserving energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ANIMATES into SETAMINA, and 'saving' (meaning except) drops its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the physical endurance to keep going.

clue.text: Inherit income — investing pound, start to produce results

parts.note: to come into money is to inherit it

indicators.note: investing here means clothing or surrounding, so the pay word wraps the pound letter

parts.note: pay is income, wages
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An heir's income, once a pound is invested, starts to bring returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's financial 'investing' really means enclosing: PAY goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: When factors come into play they begin to take effect and influence an outcome.

clue.text: Switch positions, about to return for sale

parts.note: a switch has two positions, on and off

indicators.note: return says the letters are turned back

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone changes jobs, about to come back for a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' looks like changing jobs, but it means the two settings of a light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on offer are available to buy, often at a reduced price.

clue.text: Female member of police personnel

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
staff are the personnel of an organisation

explanation.surface: A woman officer among the police workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: The distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spindle used in spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaff as an adjective means relating to women, as in the distaff side of a family.

clue.text: That place gracious ex-president tours officially

indicators.note: the president's name goes round the other pieces, as one tours a place

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US president
there means in that place
cor and gracious are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A gracious former president formally tours that place on an official visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is the exclamation 'Gracious!', matching the British exclamation 'Cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something for the record means stating it formally so that it is noted publicly.

clue.text: Sculptor in article found in Bild holding soft stone base

indicators.note: the article word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ein is the German indefinite article, as would be found in the German paper Bild
P is the music abbreviation piano, soft
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A sculptor featured in a German tabloid's article about a soft stone pedestal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bild is a German newspaper, hinting at a German word. Jacob Epstein was a modernist sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British artist famous for bronze and carved stone figures.

clue.text: Retailer cut supply in workspace

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a supple or flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order
cut says the tail letter is clipped off

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper reduces deliveries to the shop floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb of supple, bending the letters into ATELIER after 'cut' trims RETAILER's last R.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, the room where they work.

clue.text: Went carefully like this into room facing west

indicators.note: in an across entry, facing west means reading right to left
the like-this word goes into the room word

parts.note: a den is a small private room
so means thus, like this

explanation.surface: Someone creeps cautiously into a west-facing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts SO in DEN, giving DESON, which 'facing west' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to move slowly and cautiously, as a car noses out of a junction.

clue.text: Old composer knowing about a modern one

parts.note: J S Bach was a Baroque composer

indicators.note: the knowing word goes about the A

parts.note: arch means knowing, slyly mischievous

explanation.surface: An old composer is knowledgeable about a contemporary one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'composer': Burt Bacharach wrote popular songs in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Burt Bacharach was a twentieth-century songwriter, so a recent composer by contrast with the Baroque master.

clue.text: Church reluctant to store half of priest's old shroud

indicators.note: the church and reluctance pieces keep the priestly half stored between them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth means unwilling, reluctant

indicators.note: half of keeps the front half of the priest's title

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A church is unwilling to keep half of a priest's old burial cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Church reluctant' as an unwilling church, but they are two separate pieces with the priest's half stored between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerecloth was waxed cloth formerly used to wrap a corpse for burial, a winding sheet.

clue.text: It may hold crude pig, perhaps, receiving large cheers

indicators.note: the pig word receives the other letters inside it

parts.note: an oinker is a playful name for a pig, the animal that oinks
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A rude, piggish fellow is greeted with loud cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' looks like coarse behaviour, but here it means crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker ship carries unrefined petroleum, known as crude, in its holds.

clue.text: Hero's beloved Portia ultimately stops Shylock

indicators.note: the last letter plugs the gap inside the lender word

parts.note: Shylock is the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, so a lender

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Portia

explanation.surface: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia finally halts Shylock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is not a brave person but Hero of Sestos, the priestess in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his lover Hero, until he drowned.

clue.text: Twirling chanteuse is suavely entertaining Victorians?

indicators.note: Twirling says the hidden letters are read backwards
the three words entertain, i.e. hold within them, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A twirling singer smoothly entertains an audience from the Victorian era.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'entertaining' as part of the definition, but it is the signal that the words hold the answer. 'Victorians' are not 19th-century Britons but people from the Australian state of Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Australian state of Victoria are Australians, informally called by the shortened national nickname.

clue.text: King's wife going around east in cutter

indicators.note: the queen's name goes around the east letter

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of King Henry VIII
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A queen travels round the east in a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' is a sailing vessel in the surface but a cutting tool here.
explanation.definitionFit: A parer is a knife or tool for trimming the skin off fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: Proper person wanting a turnip in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means agitated and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prim individual is put out by not having a turnip for the stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with strict, prudish moral standards, scrupulously proper.

clue.text: Game 3s play with Italy — sense it's very costly

parts.note: the answer to 3 is a South African rugby player, so the game is RU, rugby union
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture with Italy, someone reasons, would be a costly affair.
explanation.walkthrough: '3s' sends you to 3 down: Springboks play rugby union, abbreviated RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous causes ruin, typically by being disastrously expensive.

clue.text: Communicates with setter, cracking e.g. Elgar and Dada minus one answer

indicators.note: the setter's letter cracks open the other word and sits inside it
minus says one answer letter is taken away

parts.note: Elgar and Dada are crossword setters' pseudonyms, i.e. aliases
A is the abbreviation for answer
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A setter talks with others, cracking clues by Elgar and Dada.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar (Telegraph Toughie) and Dada (Guardian) are crossword setters' pen names. 'minus' takes the first A from ALIASES, leaving LIASES, and 'cracking' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact with others, a form of communication.

clue.text: Idiot over the pond making chit-chat half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut keeps the front half of the word, the rest cut away

parts.note: schmoozing is chatting idly or ingratiatingly

explanation.surface: A drunken idiot across the Atlantic makes small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' means drunk in British slang, but here it removes the second half of SCHMOOZING.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmo is American slang for a stupid or contemptible person; 'over the pond' marks it as American.

clue.text: Joker I caught, holding ace of hearts

parts.note: a card is a joker, an amusing person

indicators.note: the I and C pieces hold the ace letter between them

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A card game: I'm caught holding the ace of hearts and a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace of hearts' looks like a single card, but 'of hearts' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the adjective relating to the heart, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: It gave us chutzpah when hobby's rejected by looker

indicators.note: by places the reversed hobby beside the looker word
rejected says the hobby letters are turned back

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is a hobby; the 's is 'is'
a dish is an attractive person, a looker

explanation.surface: Someone shows nerve when their pastime is spurned by a good-looking partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DIY into YID, followed by DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutzpah, meaning audacity, entered English from the Jewish language of Central and Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Better run, inhaling oxygen in the fresh air

indicators.note: the other pieces breathe the oxygen letter in between them

parts.note: to better someone is to outdo them
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A runner improves performance by breathing oxygen outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor activities take place outside, in the open air rather than in a building.

clue.text: Peer hard through windows? It's a source of drama

parts.note: an aristo is an aristocrat, a peer

indicators.note: the hard letter goes through the panes word

parts.note: panes are sheets of glass in windows
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A nobleman peers hard through windows — a dramatic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning look, which fits the windows, but it is the nobleman noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the great comic playwright of ancient Athens, whose plays are foundational in theatre.
